title: Docs: refresh tool calling (single + parallel), add partial-args note, link canonical examples
author: Wei Chen
description:
Summary: This updates the Tool Calling docs to match the canonical example patterns across SDKs and fixes the most common misunderstanding we see in support: trying to JSON.parse tool arguments during streaming before the args are complete ("partial args"). The page now includes: (1) single tool example, (2) parallel tools example (multiple tool calls in one assistant turn), and (3) a dedicated callout explaining argument delta semantics + safe aggregation.

Why: We’ve had multiple reports of users copying older snippets and hitting parse errors when tool_call arguments arrive incrementally (especially in TS). The previous docs also mixed “function calling” and “tool calling” terminology and had a legacy snippet that assumed a single tool call and complete args.

What changed (high level): Updated docs copy + code blocks for Python/TypeScript/Go; clarified event semantics for streaming tool_call deltas; added a "Partial tool args" warning + recommended accumulation pattern; added a parallel tools section with concurrency guidance; replaced legacy snippets; added links to redwood-examples canonical repo paths; aligned terminology with PM-612.

Key behavior notes added to the docs: Tool call arguments may arrive as multiple deltas; do not attempt to parse/validate until the tool call is finalized; you must accumulate by tool_call_id (or equivalent) and only parse once complete; parallel tools can produce interleaved deltas for different tool_call_id values; always enforce an allowlist and validate arguments before executing any tool.

Docs pages touched: - Guides > Tools: rewritten examples + new callouts - API Reference cross-links: updated anchors / wording for tools vs functions - Troubleshooting: new entry for "JSON parse errors during tool calling" linking back to partial-args note

Links: - Canonical examples repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples (Tools section) - Related gateway semantics alignment: ENG-2848

Testing: Docs build + link check. Snippets in this PR are copied from the canonical examples PR to reduce future drift; separate snippet-test CI runs in redwood-examples (ENG-2847).

Follow-ups (not in this PR): 1) Add a short note to Quickstarts that tools args are streamed (ENG-2849) 2) Expand troubleshooting to mention proxy buffering affecting tool streams (ENG-2850)

Release notes (user-facing): Docs: tool calling examples updated; added guidance for streaming partial tool arguments; clarified parallel tools handling; links to canonical examples.
commits: docs(tools): replace legacy tool calling snippet w/ canonical patterns
docs(tools): add parallel tool calling section + interleaving note
docs(troubleshooting): add entry for partial tool args + parse failures
docs(copy): unify terminology (tool calling), update cross-links
review_conversation:
Elliot Price (review): Can we make the “partial args” warning more explicit? People are literally calling JSON.parse on every delta; I want the docs to say “DON’T parse until finalized” in plain language.

Wei Chen (author): Yep. Added a Warning callout right above the streaming snippets, includes a short “bad vs good” explanation and the recommended accumulation approach. Also added a link from Troubleshooting back to that callout.

Henry Cho (review): For parallel tools: can we clarify that multiple tool calls can be returned in one assistant turn and that deltas may interleave? Also, wording: “tool calling” vs “function calling” should be consistent per PM-612.

Wei Chen (author): Updated section header to “Parallel tools (multiple tool calls)”, added a note about interleaving deltas by tool_call_id, and replaced remaining “function calling” mentions.

Dana Lo (review): The TS snippet should not imply that tool args is always valid JSON during streaming. Also please avoid suggesting unbounded Promise.all; users will DDOS themselves if they map tool calls to external APIs.

Wei Chen (author): Agreed. Updated TS snippet commentary to say args may be partial and must be accumulated; added concurrency guidance (limit parallelism) and a note to validate args + enforce allowlist.

Marcus Lin (security review): Please add a sentence that examples intentionally avoid shell/network tools and that production code should validate + allowlist tool names. Also avoid any text that implies executing model-provided tool names directly.

Wei Chen (author): Added a “Safety” note in both single + parallel sections: enforce allowlist, validate args, never execute arbitrary tool names, avoid dangerous tools in examples.

Brian Murphy (API): Small API nit: we should avoid claiming a specific event name in docs unless it’s stable across SDKs; frame it as “tool_call deltas” and “final tool call” rather than a literal string token.

Wei Chen (author): Updated language to be SDK-agnostic; examples still show what the SDK yields, but narrative uses generic terms.

Elliot Price (final): Looks good now. Please add a link to canonical examples repo near the top so readers immediately find runnable code.

Wei Chen (author): Added “See canonical examples” link under the first paragraph + again after the parallel section.

Approvals: Elliot Price approved; Henry Cho approved; Dana Lo approved; Marcus Lin approved.

Merge: Squash & merge.
closing_notes: Merged as part of the streaming/tools/structured output docs refresh. Coordinated wording with PM-612 and added partial-args guidance per SUP-18455/ENG-2848. Next: align quickstarts/templates to point here + canonical examples (ENG-2849).
